summary: Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (BA ~1955–1959) and the University of Washington (PhD ~1960–1968), and served as Professor of Anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).
Mengqiu Tian works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. After earning a master's at Heidelberg University (2019–2022), Tian became an FWO PhD research fellow at Ghent University in 2025.

Merab Mamardashvili was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Meredith Borthwick was an indologist and historian who earned degrees from the University of Melbourne (BA/MA ~1968–1973) and the Australian National University (PhD ~1974–1980). In 1980, she served as head at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980) and also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.

Mervyn Sprung was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at the University of Manitoba (BA), University of Toronto (MA), and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD, 1939), he served as Professor of Philosophy at Brock University (1965–1979).
Mery Cecconi is an Indologist pursuing doctoral research at Leiden University under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Mette Halskov Hansen is a sinologist who completed an MPhil at the University of Oslo (2020–2022). She worked as a research assistant at Aarhus University (2022–2023) and is attested as a professor at the University of Oslo in 2026.

Michael Alram is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. After earning his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna, he held leadership roles at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (1982–2020) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2022).

Michael Aris was a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. He held positions at the University of Oxford, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, and Harvard University.

Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn (–1988) and served as Central Asia Specialist at the Royal Library of Berlin from 1988 to 2019.

Michael Baumgarten was a religious studies scholar who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin and at Kiel University. He held academic posts at Kiel University (~1839–1845) and as Professor of Theology at the University of Rostock (1850–1858).

Michael Baxandall was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, the Courtauld Institute of Art, UC Berkeley, and Cornell University.

Michael Bernays studied under Adolf Holtzmann and attended the universities of Bonn and Heidelberg. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).
Michael Brunner is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied for a Bachelor of Arts at the University of Michigan (2024–2026) and served as Abbot at One River Zen in 2021.
Michael C. Shapiro is an Indologist and linguist who served as a professor at the University of Washington from ~1974 to 2017, becoming Professor Emeritus of Hindi in ~2017.

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford, he lectured at Oxford and LSE before serving as Professor of Anthropology at Durham University.
